content:
Apple celebrates its 50th anniversary this year, and many of its customers are even older. The company has set up a new support page listing 50 ways to make its devices easier to use, most of which involve accessibility settings.

These methods cover a wide range, from adjusting the text size on Apple Watch to having your iPhone remind you when the washing machine has finished a cycle...

Apple says the company's goal is to make its technology accessible to everyone, including elderly users.

At Apple, we believe the best technology should serve everyone, including older adults. That's why our products and services are designed with inclusivity in mind — with built-in accessibility features that help you connect, create, and do what you love in the way that suits you best. As life takes you through different stages, the way you interact with the world changes. From enlarging on-screen text to making conversations clearer in a noisy restaurant, Apple's ecosystem of devices, features, and services is designed to be flexible and adapt to your needs.

The support page focuses on accessibility features and is divided into ten main categories.

  • Vision: View screen content more comfortably
  • Hearing: Have conversations, receive alerts, and stay aware of your surroundings
  • Mobility: Adjust how you navigate and control your devices
  • Speech: Express yourself in the way you prefer
  • Cognitive: Stay focused and in control
  • Personalisation: Make it yours
  • Organisation: Remember what matters
  • Health: Stay on top of your wellbeing with practical information
  • Safety: Enjoy peace of mind
  • Communication: Stay connected

Take the Vision category as an example. It includes features like enlarging text, bolding text, inverting colours, applying colour filters, reducing transparency, boosting contrast, and reducing flicker. Some features — such as Sound Recognition — were heavily promoted by Apple when first launched but remain little-known to this day.

Sound Recognition listens for specific sounds and uses on-device intelligence to notify you when it detects them. It can recognise 15 different sounds, and you can also train your device to recognise your own name as well as unique electronic sounds in your environment, such as beeps from kitchen appliances, certain types of alarms, or doorbells. Sound Recognition on HomePod can even detect the sound of smoke or carbon monoxide alarms. Sound Recognition also works with CarPlay, where your iPhone listens for and detects things like sirens, horns, and even a baby crying. Once a specific sound is detected, you'll receive a notification — and if you're using CarPlay, the notification will appear on your car's display.

The page is an impressively comprehensive summary of the many accessibility features currently available across Apple's range of devices. Each section provides individual guidance for every supported device, which depending on the feature may include iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Vision Pro, and CarPlay.
